newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Eight police die in mystery Bogota blast.
newsitem.headline: Eight police die in mystery Bogota blast.

text.p: Eight policemen were killed and more than 10 others were injured on Tuesday in a powerful explosion in the parking lot of a police station on the southwest outskirts of Bogota, authorities said.

Metropolitan Police chief Teodoro Campo said the explosion occurred at in the back of a truck that was being searched in the police station's parking lot on suspicion that it had been loaded with contraband goods.
"We have a total of eight dead and more than 10 wounded," Campo told reporters, adding that some of the injured had lost limbs or suffered other life-threatening injuries.
He said he could not rule out the possibility that a potent bomb, probably dynamite, was placed aboard the truck by leftist guerrillas or drug traffickers.
But Campo stopped short of saying the explosion was directed against the police, since the truck had been taken to the police station for inspection after being confiscated elsewhere.

National Police director Gen. Rosso Jose Serrano said victims of the blast included three crack police intelligence officers. In all, two police majors, a captain, three lieutenants and two patrolmen were killed, police said.

Speculation in the local media was that a possible remote controlled bomb was detonated by guerrillas or powerful drug traffickers who wanted to sow terror ahead of a key congressional vote on Thursday on whether to lift Colombia's constitutional ban on extradition for drug traffickers.
Police arrested Jose Anibal Sanchez, the truck's driver.
Looking dazed in an interview with local television, the trucker said he had been hired by an unidentified client in the capital to carry an unknown cargo to Colombia's northern province of Bolivar.
Colombia has the highest murder rate in Latin America and police have been on the frontline of victims.
In March, the head of the judicial police said a total of 4,617 police officers had been killed in Colombia since 1990, the most anywhere in the world.
